deliverables: Ongoing maintenance: bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra readiness including Plutus V4 support, ledger rules, transaction-builder updates, conformance testing, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin interoperability including Spring Boot and Ktor examples and cleaner integration with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Foundational runtime components including reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
Reference applications, integration tests, early-user feedback, public reporting, third-party assurance, and milestone-based delivery
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm, and its components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The proposal requests ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, equivalent to about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.

The proposal is a reduced resubmission of a prior Scalus proposal, cutting the ask from ₳8.503 million to about ₳2.465 million, reducing duration from 12 to 9 months, reducing FTE from 8.25 to 2.25, and removing the standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, and broad formal verification from scope.
Delivery is proposed to be milestone-based through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
The proposal says Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js reaches more than 20,000 monthly downloads.

Dijkstra readiness is presented as necessary because the hard fork introduces Plutus V4 support, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affecting smart contract development, evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and workflows.

The proposed application runtime would add an operating layer for following chain data, reacting to on-chain events, scheduling time-based actions, coordinating backend workflows, and recovering from failure.

The proposal claims Scalus aligns with Cardano 2030 mainly as enabling infrastructure for developer experience, interoperability, education, talent development, and ecosystem growth rather than by directly producing TVL, transactions, or users.
Lantr Engineering says it has delivered every prior Scalus milestone on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus over 9 months, emphasizing maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, ecosystem interoperability, and a bounded application runtime, with several adoption and delivery claims that are partly asserted and partly externally checkable.
